Synopsis:
    Iran announces an imminent new restricted maritime zone in the Gulf and a new Iran-Oman managed shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. This follows resumed tit-for-tat strikes between U.S. and Iranian forces on tankers and warships. The Strait is near-closed to normal tanker traffic (~10 ships/day, multi-month low), with Brent crude at ~$97/bbl (+0.8%). Iran's economy is under severe stress from U.S. sanctions and oil export blockade (active since mid-April), though Tehran signals defiance. A June ceasefire has collapsed. The U.S. claims partial success keeping ~9 mbpd flowing via the Strait plus bypass pipelines (~two-thirds of pre-conflict levels). U.S. elections in November add political pressure. Escalation risk remains high with no diplomatic resolution in sight.

The stalemate and ceasefire collapse add further uncertainty to the forward outlook.
